repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `--monokernel`, as on gfx950.

The PR was rebased onto `main` after #61082 as one commit. The commits after it merge `main` and answer the second review (see Details). gfx942 now runs the same layers whole as gfx950, with the switch of #61082 (see Details). The latest commits take the PR out of shared code, as RFC #60904 asks, and merge `main` with #62131 (see Details). The AgentX and GSM8K comparisons below are from 67206b7 and the commits before it, when the switch was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. The checks of the latest commits are at the end of Validation.

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×).
- A standard decoder layer takes 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 on average (pooled p 0.49). The difference is not significant.
- On a2ce22d7e317 at concurrency 7, GPQA-Diamond is 85.0%, AIME25 99.0% and RULER NIAH 40 of 40 in every cell, against 85.3%, 99.4% and 40 of 40 for the reference arm of #60397 on MI355X.
- The gfx942 code runs only with `--monokernel`, on gfx942. Outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and the tests, the PR adds an 8-line hook to the DSpark speculator and two CI jobs.
- On gfx950 all 76 builds of the mono kernels, the 12 of the DSpark draft's runner included, have the same register and LDS use as on `main` and the same count of each instruction, apart from 1 or 2 more `s_waitcnt` in K2 and the FFN launch. The draft runner's scratch is now laid out for its MoE, see Details.
- On MI355X with `--monokernel` at TP2, two runs of each arm on 6caadd0, before #62131: GSM8K strict match 0.9257 and 0.9242 against 0.9249 and 0.9272 for `main` (see Validation).

## Limits on gfx942

- TP4 only. At TP2 the path logs one line and every layer runs vLLM's path.
- Decode steps of up to 42 rows, which is 7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950, so a GEMV pass takes 6 tokens instead of 16. A larger step, prefill, a mixed step and a PIECEWISE graph run vLLM's path on every layer and every rank.
- gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8, so the kernels read their own copies of the weights. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB. On MI325X with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache still holds 11.18 million tokens. MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well, so the numbers here are for MI325X.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on MI325X, TP4. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`. The PR arm is the same image with the `vllm/` changes of #60397 and this PR copied over its `vllm` package. Both arms use the same command and environment, apart from the switch, which was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` on those commits.

**AgentX, concurrency 1, against `main`.** One 3,600 s run per arm, each on a fresh server.

| | `main` | PR | PR / `main` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured requests, no errors | 239 | 306 | |
| Interactivity P50 (tokens/s/user) | 216.85 | 503.53 | 2.32× |
| Interactivity P90 (tokens/s/user) | 182.25 | 411.26 | 2.26× |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 0.510 | 0.544 | |
| Total throughput per GPU (tokens/s) | 4,024 | 6,546 | 1.63× |

**AgentX, concurrency 2, 4 and 8.** There is no `main` run at these concurrencies, so the reference is InferenceX's published MI325X TP4 points ([Actions run 35637516947](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35637516947)). They come from an older nightly. At concurrency 1 the published P90 is 189.90, close to our `main` run.

| Concurrency | P90, published | P90, PR | Throughput per GPU, published | Throughput per GPU, PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 153.22 | 368.64 (2.41×) | 4,255 | 6,729 (1.58×) |
| 4 | 142.75 | 316.28 (2.22×) | 6,315 | 8,882 (1.41×) |
| 8 | 81.52 | 162.61 (1.99×) | 10,998 | 14,839 (1.35×) |

At concurrency 8, steps of more than 42 rows ran vLLM's path during 0.14% of the decode time.

**Accuracy.** `lm_eval` `gsm8k`, 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, greedy, DSpark with block rejection. At concurrency 7 every decode step of this PR takes the mono path. Strict match of each run:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1 | 0.9340, 0.9318 | 0.9272 |
| Concurrency 7 | 0.9242, 0.9257, 0.9242 | 0.9295, 0.9242, 0.9265, 0.9303 |

Two runs of the same code differ by up to 0.6 points, so the runs are pooled with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with one stratum a question. At concurrency 7 this PR scores 0.23 points more than `main` (p 0.49). Over all runs the mono path scores 0.14 points less (p 0.54). The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, where vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.

**GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and RULER NIAH.** A build of a2ce22d7e317 with `--monokernel` at TP4 and concurrency 7, with the sample counts of #60397: GPQA-Diamond with 2 option orders and 4 seeds at up to 32K tokens, AIME25 with 16 seeds at up to 64K tokens, and NIAH with `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples a cell. The reference is the MI355X result of #60397. The runs are in the comments [for NIAH](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6178954285), [for AIME25](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6182853591) and [for GPQA-Diamond](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6191592654).

| | This PR, MI325X TP4 | #60397 mono, MI355X TP2 | #60397 reference, MI355X TP2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA-Diamond | 85.0% (1347 of 1584) | 85.1 ± 2.2% | 85.3 ± 2.2% |
| AIME25 | 99.0% (475 of 480) | 98.3 ± 0.8% | 99.4 ± 0.3% |
| RULER NIAH, 9 cells | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each |

A debugging patch, not part of this PR, ran vLLM's own layer after each mono layer on the same inputs, in steps of 6 to 42 rows. No output had a non-finite value, and the index layers' top-512 lists matched vLLM's in all 481,944 entries.

**gfx950.** `main` and this PR on the same MI355X node, two runs each, in the order PR, `main`, `main`, PR. All four runs use `--monokernel` at TP2, DSpark with 5 drafts, probabilistic drafts and block rejection, and the same server arguments (see Reproduce). `main` is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1`, and the PR runs use the same image with this PR's files at 6caadd0 copied in. At 6caadd0 the PR still held a change of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` that it no longer has (see Changes outside the model directory), and `main` did not have #62131 yet. The speed rows use random prompts of 1024 tokens and 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at concurrency 1 and 64 at concurrency 8.

| | `main`, run 1 | `main`, run 2 | This PR, run 1 | This PR, run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, strict match | 0.9249 | 0.9272 | 0.9257 | 0.9242 |
| Concurrency 1, output throughput (tokens/s) | 520.34 | 579.54 | 584.43 | 577.95 |
| Concurrency 1, median TPOT (ms) | 1.59 | 1.56 | 1.54 | 1.48 |
| Concurrency 1, median ITL (ms) | 7.60 | 7.59 | 7.36 | 7.38 |
| Concurrency 1, median TTFT (ms) | 66.30 | 66.55 | 67.09 | 67.02 |
| Concurrency 8, output throughput (tokens/s) | 2038.63 | 1986.51 | 2049.16 | 2099.40 |
| Concurrency 8, median TPOT (ms) | 3.37 | 3.35 | 3.47 | 3.17 |
| Concurrency 8, median ITL (ms) | 17.06 | 16.99 | 16.84 | 16.77 |
| Concurrency 8, median TTFT (ms) | 84.37 | 83.77 | 84.51 | 83.91 |

GSM8K is the same within the spread of the runs, and the median TTFT differs by less than 1 ms. With DSpark a decode step streams several tokens, so the median ITL is the time of one decode step. It was about 0.2 ms shorter with the PR, from that `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change. The TPOT also depends on how many drafts are accepted. In the first `main` run a few first tokens took more than a second, which lowered its throughput at concurrency 1.

**Tests.** The kernel tests are in `tests/kernels/models/amd/` and run in a new one-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. A new four-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` runs the real-model and graph replay tests on gfx942 at TP4. On MI325X all of them pass on 6cb1400, and the two TP4 files take about 10 minutes. On MI355X the two TP4 files pass their CDNA4 cases on 0597d94 too, and their gfx942 cases skip there.

| File | Compared against |
|---|---|
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_topk.py` | vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` and its candidate mask, for contexts from 100 to 300,000 tokens |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_cand_logits.py` | AITER's dense logits at the candidate positions, bit for bit |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_sparse_indexer.py` | vLLM's ROCm indexer op on a decode step, for a layer without candidate blocks, for layer 20, which writes them, and for a layer that reads them. The gfx942 indexer layer runs its own copy of that op's decode path, and this test fails when the two stop agreeing |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` | the old SWA metadata ops and top-k packing, on 800 random batches |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` | vLLM's Markov sampling loop, and each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's logits, exactly |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_draft_lm_head.py` | an fp32 GEMM. It also checks that `wvSplitK` gets no 5-row GEMM with `--monokernel` and keeps it without |
| `test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py` | torch references for K2's key lists, the first layer's seam, the GEMV cores and the gfx942 FP4 and FP8 conversions |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` | vLLM's own decoder layers in a five-layer model with random weights, at TP4 with the FP8 indexer, at steps of 8 rows (two GEMV passes, the second one padded) and 42 rows (the limit), every layer at every decode step |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` | the composed runner at TP4 on the copies made at load: the padded step against its rows run alone, and 300 replays of steps of 6, 8 and 42 rows in one CUDA graph against the first run, bit for bit |

On f0a549d a TP4 server with the mono path also answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9303, 0.9272 and 0.9257. On the rebased commit pre-commit passes, and the 60 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU. On a2ce22d7e317, which merges `main` into the rebased commit, the new MI300 job passes in CI, and a TP4 server with the mono path ran GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and NIAH (see Accuracy). The commits after it merge `main` again and follow four changes on `main`: #58689, which renamed the V4.1 ROCm attention classes, #55090, which split the skinny GEMM check, #58800, which moved the gfx1250 check out of `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`, and #61161, which mixes the draft step into the seed of the draft sampler. The fused Markov launch now mixes in its draft step too, so its draft tokens stay the same as those of vLLM's loop.

The latest commits move the gfx942 top-k launches into an indexer layer in the model folder, add a test that compares that layer with vLLM's indexer op, drop the `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change, and merge `main` with #62131. On 6cb1400 pre-commit passes, the 76 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU, and the kernel tests and the two TP4 files pass on MI325X with the ROCm 7.2 nightly and with the ROCm 10 nightly. The new indexer test fails on a copy of the layer whose logits take the head weights of the wrong rows. With the ROCm 7.2 nightly a TP4 server with the mono path answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9310, 0.9303 and 0.9295. With the ROCm 10 nightly such a server also answered the sanity prompts correctly, and GSM8K gave 0.9295, 0.9272 and 0.9242. In one of three starts with the mono path on ROCm 10 the server hung before it was ready: three ranks stopped in AITER's custom all-reduce while it registered the buffers of the decoder replay CUDA graphs, which `main` also captures. On gfx950 the 76 builds compile, see Claims, and on MI355X a TP2 server with the mono path ran the DSpark draft layers whole with the fix of #62131's scratch and answered the sanity prompts correctly.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server, the same for both arms apart from `--monokernel`, which the `main` arm leaves out:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_FLYDSL_QR_INT4=1
export VLLM_DSV41_FUSED_COMBINE_TOPK_SWA=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

GSM8K uses `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` instead of the two synthetic keys, with `lm_eval` 0.4.9.2 and `num_concurrent=1` for the concurrency 1 runs:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=7,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512,temperature=0.0,top_p=1.0
```

AgentX is the InferenceX AgentX client ([agentx-standalone.md](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/docs/agentx-standalone.md)) with the arguments of the InferenceX AgentX sweep and `--concurrency 1`, 2, 4 or 8. InferenceX's `python -m infx.results.agentic.process_agentic_result` scored each run with `TP=4 GPU_COUNT=4`.

The gfx950 runs, with the same server for both arms:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

The speed rows are `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, with `--max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 16` and with `--max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 64`. GSM8K is the `lm_eval` command above with `num_concurrent=8` and `--gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048`.

Kernel tests on one GPU, and the TP4 tests on four:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/models/amd/
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py
```

</details>

## Details

- **Layers.** gfx942 runs every backbone layer whole, as gfx950 does since #61082. The index layers use vLLM's FP8 indexer, because the MXFP4 indexer cache needs CDNA4. vLLM's compressor and indexer run between K1 and K2, as on gfx950. On gfx942 `mono/keylist.py` then writes the layer's key lists, so K2 is the build without the key table. On gfx942 the 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch after vLLM's attention, built for the draft's 128 experts and top 3, on the target's runner. On gfx950 they run whole on a runner of their own, as #62131 added.
- **gfx942 helper ops** in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`: the sparse indexer's decode top-512 (`topk512_gfx942.cu`) and its candidate logits, the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each, and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step. With `--monokernel` on gfx942 the V4.1 ROCm attention takes the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. It runs vLLM's ROCm indexer op on every step except a step of only decode rows, which runs the decode path of that op with the top-k launches in front of vLLM's ops. The DSpark speculator asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, and the DSv4.1 draft model runs the fused Markov launches there. `draft_lm_head.py` pads the DSpark draft's 5-row logits GEMM to 6 rows, so that vLLM's dispatch takes the torch GEMM instead of `wvSplitK`. For the 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard that takes 96 µs instead of 295 µs on MI325X. Each helper leaves a call it cannot take to vLLM's own op. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops.
- **Weight copies.** The routed experts are copied in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. The copies are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold their addresses.
- **Changes outside the model directory.** One hook in the DSpark speculator: `_sample_sequential` asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, if the model has one, and runs its own loop when the call returns False. Only the DSv4.1 draft model has one, and it takes a step only with `--monokernel` on gfx942. The rest are the two CI jobs. The earlier hooks in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` are now the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. The change of the padding loops of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` is dropped, because #58633 parallelises the same padding.
- **Merge of #62131.** #62131 runs the DSpark draft layers whole on gfx950, on a runner of their own whose MoE takes one FP4 group an ug task (`DRAFT_UG_GROUPS`). Its scratch was laid out for the default two groups, and with one group the ug flags take twice the room. So the flags of the upper half of the tasks were written over the start of the `normed` rows that the MoE reads as its input, at TP 2 and 4 and for every step width. Only the draft layers could be affected, not the target's output, and in a GSM8K check on MI355X `main` accepted as many drafts as this PR, so the overlap did not show there. `scratch_layout` and `scratch_bytes` now take the runner's groups. `run_ffn` checks that each MoE region of a build fits the layout, and that check found the overlap when the draft runner's K2 was built. The FFN launch reads the target's layout, because it runs on the target's runner, also for a gfx942 draft layer.
- **Since the first review.** The branch is rebased onto `main` as one commit. The gfx942 ops moved from `vllm/model_executor/layers/dsv41_gfx942/` into `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`, as RFC #60904 asks for model kernels. `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW` and its layer-by-layer check are removed. The rebase onto #61082 takes its switch and its layer plan on gfx942 too. That removes the gfx942 paths of their own for the first layer, the window layers and the index layers, apart from `mono/keylist.py`.
- **Since the second review.** The kernel tests moved to `tests/kernels/models/amd/`. The fused Markov test checks each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's cached logits. The change to vLLM's skinny GEMM dispatch is reverted, and only the DSpark draft's lm_head avoids `wvSplitK`, with `--monokernel` on gfx942. `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` and a gfx942 graph replay test in `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` run at TP4 in a new four-GPU MI300 job. On gfx942 the first layer's output bound in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` is 6% instead of 3%, because vLLM's gfx942 MoE keeps bf16 activations and the kernels quantize them to MXFP8, which alone moves the FFN output of the test's random weights by 4.65%. The residual stream then differs by up to 2.5% instead of 0.4 to 0.7%, so past the first layer a routing near-tie there is a gap of up to 0.02 instead of 0.01, and up to a third of the tokens may flip an expert instead of a quarter (22% seen).
- **Relation to other PRs.** Draft #61482 moves the FlyDSL stages to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`, and this PR edits the files it moves. Whichever of the two merges second needs a rebase. If this PR merges first, its gfx942 tests can check #61482's move on MI325X. #62131 is merged into this branch, see Merge of #62131. #58633 parallelises the padding of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, which this PR changed until the latest commits, and neither PR needs the other. #61311 moves `amd/mono/` to `amd/specialized_decode/mono/` and replaces `mono_decode.py`, as RFC #60904 describes. A trial merge of the two conflicts in 15 files, among them `mono_decode.py` and `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, which #61311 deletes and this PR changes. So whichever of the two merges second needs a port. #61869 adds a fused Markov sampler at the start of `_sample_sequential`, next to this PR's hook, and the two merge there without a conflict.
- **Follow-ups.** Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 drafts also take the mono path. One copy of the routed experts instead of two. Other TP sizes on gfx942. The whole DSpark draft layers on gfx942, as on gfx950. `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled op in `csrc/`.

---

detail.title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on MI300X and MI325X (gfx942)

files.patch:
@@ -1072,3 +1072,27 @@ steps:

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""cand_logits.candidate_logits against AITER's dense
+deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits, called the way vLLM's decode indexer calls it
+on gfx942 (rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits).
+
+For one decode request of 6 rows, every compact logit and id must be
+bit-identical to the dense logit gathered at the same candidate position,
+with -inf and id -1 where a candidate block is -1 or a position is at or past
+the row's end. The top 512 of the compact rows must then be the top 512 that
+candidate_top_k_512 takes from the dense rows within the candidate blocks.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _on_gfx942(), reason="the kernel reproduces AITER's gfx942 kernel"
+)
+
+ROWS, DIM, PAGE = 6, 128, 64
+MAX_MODEL_LEN = 1 << 20
+CAND_BLOCKS, CAND_BLOCK = 2048, 8
+
+
+def _make_inputs(ctx: int, heads: int):
+    """FP8 queries, head weights, row lengths, block tables and a paged
+    indexer cache of FP8 keys and FP32 key scales. Row r is the request's
+    token at position ctx - ROWS + r and sees the keys up to its own
+    position."""
+    from aiter import dtypes
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    q = (torch.randn(ROWS, 1, heads, DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    weights = torch.randn(ROWS, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    context_lens = torch.arange(
+        ctx - ROWS + 1, ctx + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    used = (ctx + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    num_pages = used + 64
+    tables = torch.zeros(ROWS, MAX_MODEL_LEN // PAGE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    tables[:, :used] = torch.randperm(num_pages, device="cuda")[:used].to(torch.int32)
+    vals = (torch.randn(num_pages, PAGE * DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    scales = torch.rand(num_pages, PAGE, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    kv = torch.cat([vals.view(torch.uint8), scales.view(torch.uint8)], dim=1)
+    return q, weights, context_lens, tables, kv.view(num_pages, PAGE, 1, DIM + 4)
+
+
+def _make_candidates(context_lens: torch.Tensor, gen) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Distinct candidate blocks of each row in random order, with the row's
+    newest block among them and -1 padding where a row has fewer than 2048
+    blocks. Row 1 also gets -1 in a few places in the middle, as layer 20
+    writes for a block whose score is -inf."""
+    cand = torch.full((ROWS, CAND_BLOCKS), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for r in range(ROWS):
+        blocks = (int(context_lens[r]) + CAND_BLOCK - 1) // CAND_BLOCK
+        if blocks <= CAND_BLOCKS:
+            picks = torch.randperm(blocks, generator=gen)
+        else:
+            others = torch.randperm(blocks - 1, generator=gen)[: CAND_BLOCKS - 1]
+            picks = torch.cat([others, torch.tensor([blocks - 1])])
+            picks = picks[torch.randperm(CAND_BLOCKS, generator=gen)]
+        cand[r, : picks.numel()] = picks.to(torch.int32)
+    cand[1, 100:105] = -1
+    return cand.cuda()
+
+
+def _gather_reference(dense, context_lens, cand):
+    """The compact rows that gatherCandidates writes from dense logits."""
+    i = torch.arange(CAND_BLOCKS * CAND_BLOCK, device=cand.device)
+    block = cand[:, i // CAND_BLOCK].long()
+    col = block * CAND_BLOCK + (i % CAND_BLOCK)[None, :]
+    live = (block >= 0) & (col < context_lens[:, None].long())
+    logits = torch.gather(dense[:ROWS], 1, torch.where(live, col, 0))
+    logits = torch.where(live, logits, float("-inf"))
+    ids = torch.where(live, col, -1).to(torch.int32)
+    return logits, ids
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_lens_2d", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [32, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ctx", [8192, 131072])
+def test_candidate_logits_bit_identical_to_dense(ctx, heads, seq_lens_2d):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import cand_logits, topk
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import paged_mqa_logits_module
+
+    aiter_logits = paged_mqa_logits_module()
+    if aiter_logits is None:
+        pytest.skip("AITER's paged MQA logits module is not installed")
+    q, weights, context_lens, tables, kv = _make_inputs(ctx, heads)
+    cand = _make_candidates(context_lens.cpu(), torch.Generator().manual_seed(1))
+    lens = context_lens.view(-1, 1) if seq_lens_2d else context_lens
+    row_len = CAND_BLOCKS * CAND_BLOCK
+    dense = torch.full((ROWS, MAX_MODEL_LEN), -1.0, device="cuda")
+    out_logits = torch.empty(ROWS, row_len, device="cuda")
+    out_ids = torch.empty(ROWS, row_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    aiter_logits.deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(
+        q,
+        kv,
+        weights,
+        dense,
+        context_lens,
+        tables,
+        MAX_MODEL_LEN,
+        ChunkK=256,
+        Preshuffle=True,
+        KVBlockSize=PAGE,
+        WavePerEU=2,
+    )
+    cand_logits.candidate_logits(
+        q.view(ROWS, heads, DIM),
+        kv,
+        weights,
+        lens,
+        1,
+        tables,
+        cand,
+        CAND_BLOCK,
+        out_logits,
+        out_ids,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref_logits, ref_ids = _gather_reference(dense, context_lens, cand)
+    assert torch.equal(ref_ids, out_ids)
+    assert torch.equal(ref_logits.view(torch.int32), out_logits.view(torch.int32))
+
+    ext = topk._load()
+    old = torch.empty(ROWS, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    new = torch.empty_like(old)
+    ext.candidate_top_k_512(dense, 1, lens, cand, CAND_BLOCK, old)
+    ext.compact_top_k_512_regs(out_logits, out_ids, lens, 1, new)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(old.sort(1).values, new.sort(1).values)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The one-launch DeepSeek-V4.1 decode metadata of gfx942 against the vLLM
+ops that it replaces.
+
+swa_decode_meta.launch replaces the decode part of the ROCm SWA metadata
+build: torch.ge for is_valid_token, the zero fill of the unused lengths,
+_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel (or the DSpark draft block's
+ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel), build_ragged_indices_from_dense and
+_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers. topk_pack.launch replaces
+compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr. For each random decode batch
+vLLM's ops run first. Then every output buffer is overwritten with -7
+(is_valid_token with its negation), the fused launch runs, and every output
+that a reader uses must be equal.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="the fused launches are for ROCm"
+)
+
+WINDOW = 128
+MAX_TOKENS = 16384
+MAX_SEQS = 128
+TOPK = 512
+
+
+def _swa_case(g, max_rows):
+    """A random decode batch. It mixes short sequences, sequences at 128k,
+    padded tokens with slot -1, a replay start inside the window, null blocks
+    (block 0) and block sizes 64 and 128. Returns None when the batch has more
+    rows than the fused launch takes."""
+    block_size = (64, 128)[int(torch.randint(0, 2, (1,), generator=g))]
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, 6, (1,), generator=g))
+    q_len = (1, 6)[int(torch.randint(0, 2, (1,), generator=g))]
+    lens = []
+    for _ in range(num_reqs):
+        kind = int(torch.randint(0, 3, (1,), generator=g))
+        if kind == 0:
+            lens.append(int(torch.randint(q_len, 140, (1,), generator=g)))
+        elif kind == 1:
+            lens.append(int(torch.randint(140, 5000, (1,), generator=g)))
+        else:
+            lens.append(131072 + int(torch.randint(0, 64, (1,), generator=g)))
+    n = num_reqs * q_len
+    if n > max_rows:
+        return None
+    max_blocks = (max(lens) + block_size - 1) // block_size + 1
+    block_table = torch.randint(
+        1, 200000, (MAX_SEQS, max_blocks), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    # The sliding window manager points blocks outside the window at the
+    # null block 0. Put some of those inside windows as well.
+    block_table[torch.rand(block_table.shape, generator=g) < 0.05] = 0
+    slot_mapping = torch.randint(0, 1 << 30, (n,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int64)
+    slot_mapping[torch.rand(n, generator=g) < 0.15] = -1
+    replay = torch.zeros(MAX_SEQS + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for r in range(num_reqs):
+        if float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.3:
+            replay[r] = max(0, lens[r] - int(torch.randint(1, 160, (1,), generator=g)))
+    return dict(
+        n=n,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        slot_mapping=slot_mapping.cuda(),
+        query_start_loc=(torch.arange(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32) * q_len).cuda(),
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32).cuda(),
+        token_to_req=(torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32) // q_len).cuda(),
+        block_table=block_table.cuda(),
+        replay_start=replay.cuda(),
+    )
+
+
+def _swa_buffers(width, noncausal):
+    """Buffers of the size that the metadata builder allocates."""
+    return dict(
+        noncausal=noncausal,
+        width=width,
+        is_valid=torch.zeros(MAX_TOKENS, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"),
+        indices=torch.zeros(MAX_TOKENS, 1, width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        lens=torch.full((MAX_TOKENS,), 5, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        ragged=torch.empty(MAX_TOKENS * width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        indptr=torch.empty(MAX_TOKENS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+    )
+
+
+def _swa_old_ops(c, b):
+    """The decode part of vLLM's SWA metadata build and its ROCm ragged
+    step."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm import _copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.sparse_swa import (
+        _COMPUTE_DSPARK_NONCAUSAL_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL,
+        _COMPUTE_SWA_INDICES_AND_LENS_KERNEL,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        build_ragged_indices_from_dense,
+    )
+
+    n, width = c["n"], b["width"]
+    is_valid = b["is_valid"][:n]
+    torch.ge(c["slot_mapping"], 0, out=is_valid)
+    b["lens"][n:] = 0
+    common = (c["query_start_loc"], c["seq_lens"], c["token_to_req"], is_valid)
+    if b["noncausal"]:
+        _COMPUTE_DSPARK_NONCAUSAL_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL(
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            WINDOW,
+            width,
+            *common,
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["block_size"],
+            num_tokens=n,
+            token_offset=0,
+        )
+    else:
+        _COMPUTE_SWA_INDICES_AND_LENS_KERNEL(
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            WINDOW,
+            width,
+            b["lens"],
+            b["lens"],
+            *common,
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["block_size"],
+            c["replay_start"],
+            num_tokens=n,
+            token_offset=0,
+        )
+    ragged, indptr = build_ragged_indices_from_dense(
+        b["indices"][:n].reshape(n, width), b["lens"][:n]
+    )
+    _copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers(ragged, indptr, b["ragged"], b["indptr"], n, width)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("noncausal", [False, True])
+def test_swa_decode_meta_matches_vllm_ops(noncausal):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import swa_decode_meta
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.compressor_utils import (
+        get_dspark_swa_index_width,
+    )
+
+    width = get_dspark_swa_index_width(WINDOW, 5) if noncausal else WINDOW
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1234)
+    failed, done = [], 0
+    while done < 300:
+        c = _swa_case(g, swa_decode_meta.MAX_ROWS)
+        if c is None:
+            continue
+        done += 1
+        n = c["n"]
+        b = _swa_buffers(width, noncausal)
+        _swa_old_ops(c, b)
+        nnz = int(b["indptr"][n])
+        want = dict(
+            is_valid=b["is_valid"][:n].clone(),
+            indices=b["indices"][:n].clone(),
+            lens=b["lens"].clone(),
+            indptr=b["indptr"][: n + 1].clone(),
+            ragged=b["ragged"][:nnz].clone(),
+        )
+        b["is_valid"][:n].copy_(~want["is_valid"])
+        for key in ("indices", "lens", "ragged", "indptr"):
+            b[key].fill_(-7)
+        swa_decode_meta.launch(
+            c["slot_mapping"],
+            b["is_valid"][:n],
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            b["ragged"],
+            b["indptr"],
+            c["query_start_loc"],
+            c["seq_lens"],
+            c["token_to_req"],
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["replay_start"],
+            n,
+            WINDOW,
+            c["block_size"],
+            noncausal=noncausal,
+        )
+        got = dict(
+            is_valid=b["is_valid"][:n],
+            indices=b["indices"][:n],
+            lens=b["lens"],
+            indptr=b["indptr"][: n + 1],
+            ragged=b["ragged"][:nnz],
+        )
+        bad = [k for k in want if not torch.equal(want[k], got[k])]
+        if bad:
+            failed.append((done, n, c["block_size"], bad))
+    assert not failed, (
+        f"batches that differ (case, rows, block size, outputs): {failed}"
+    )
+
+
+def _topk_case(g, max_rows):
+    """A decode batch of top-512 rows as the indexer writes them: valid local
+    indices first and -1 after them, some rows shorter than 512, some rows
+    with a -1 inside the valid entries, and padded tokens."""
+    n = int(torch.randint(1, max_rows + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, n + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    block_size = (32, 64, 128)[int(torch.randint(0, 3, (1,), generator=g))]
+    comp_len = int(torch.randint(1, 70000, (1,), generator=g))
+    blocks = (comp_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
+    block_table = torch.randint(
+        0, 300000, (MAX_SEQS, blocks + 1), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    topk = torch.full((n, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for t in range(n):
+        valid = min(TOPK, int(torch.randint(0, comp_len + 1, (1,), generator=g)))
+        if float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.5:
+            valid = min(TOPK, comp_len)
+        topk[t, :valid] = torch.randperm(comp_len, generator=g)[:valid].to(torch.int32)
+        if valid > 4 and float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.2:
+            topk[t, int(torch.randint(0, valid, (1,), generator=g))] = -1
+    t2r = torch.sort(torch.randint(0, num_reqs, (n,), generator=g)).values
+    is_valid = torch.rand(n, generator=g) > 0.15
+    return (
+        topk.cuda(),
+        t2r.to(torch.int32).cuda(),
+        block_table.cuda(),
+        block_size,
+        is_valid.cuda(),
+    )
+
+
+def test_topk_pack_matches_vllm():
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import rocm
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import topk_pack
+
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(4321)
+    failed = []
+    for i in range(500):
+        case = _topk_case(g, topk_pack.MAX_ROWS)
+        ref = rocm._compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr_old(*case)
+        out = topk_pack.launch(*case, poison=True)
+        nnz = int(ref[1][-1])
+        bad = [
+            name
+            for name, a, b in (
+                ("topk_lens", out[2], ref[2]),
+                ("topk_indptr", out[1], ref[1]),
+                ("global_topk_ragged", out[0][:nnz], ref[0][:nnz]),
+            )
+            if a.shape != b.shape or not torch.equal(a, b)
+        ]
+        if out[0].shape != ref[0].shape:
+            bad.append("ragged shape")
+        if bad:
+            failed.append((i, case[0].shape[0], bad))
+    assert not failed, f"batches that differ (case, rows, outputs): {failed}"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""draft_lm_head.compute_logits, the DSpark draft's base logits on gfx942.
+
+With --monokernel on gfx942, the draft's 5 rows of one request get a sixth
+row of zeros, so that vLLM's dispatch (rocm_unquantized_gemm) takes the torch
+GEMM instead of wvSplitK, and the logits of the first 5 rows come back. Every
+other row count, and every call without --monokernel, keeps vLLM's dispatch,
+which sends up to 5 rows to wvSplitK. The tests count the wvSplitK calls of
+vLLM's dispatch on the draft's lm_head shard at TP 4 and compare the logits
+with an fp32 GEMM.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="the helper is for ROCm"
+)
+
+# The DSpark draft's lm_head shard at tensor parallel size 4.
+VOCAB_SHARD, HIDDEN = 32320, 5120
+
+
+def _skip_unless_gfx942():
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    if not on_gfx942():
+        pytest.skip("the helper runs on gfx942 only")
+
+
+def _set_gate(monkeypatch, on: bool):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import ops
+
+    # The model records --monokernel when it is created. These tests have no
+    # model, so they set the recorded flag themselves.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "_monokernel", on)
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+
+
+class _LMHead(torch.nn.Module):
+    """The parts of ParallelLMHead that vLLM's GEMM dispatch uses."""
+
+    def __init__(self, w):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+            UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+        )
+
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+        self.quant_method = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+
+
+def _processor(head, x):
+    """The logits processor without its tensor parallel gather, which needs a
+    process group. The GEMM is the same."""
+    return head.quant_method.apply(head, x)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def wvsplitk_rows(monkeypatch):
+    """The row counts of the wvSplitK calls that vLLM's dispatch makes."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers import utils
+
+    rows: list[int] = []
+    real = utils.ops.wvSplitK
+
+    def counted(weight, x, *args, **kwargs):
+        rows.append(x.shape[0])
+        return real(weight, x, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils.ops, "wvSplitK", counted)
+    return rows
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("monokernel", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 4, 5, 6, 10])
+def test_draft_lm_head_takes_5_rows_off_wvsplitk(
+    monkeypatch, wvsplitk_rows, rows, monokernel
+):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import draft_lm_head
+
+    _skip_unless_gfx942()
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(rows)
+    w = torch.randn(VOCAB_SHARD, HIDDEN, generator=g, device="cuda") * 0.02
+    x = torch.randn(rows, HIDDEN, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    head = _LMHead(w.to(torch.bfloat16))
+
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=monokernel)
+    try:
+        got = draft_lm_head.compute_logits(_processor, head, x.to(torch.bfloat16))
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    finally:
+        _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=False)
+
+    # Only the 5 rows with --monokernel leave wvSplitK. Every other call
+    # keeps vLLM's dispatch, which takes wvSplitK for up to 5 rows.
+    padded = monokernel and rows == draft_lm_head.ROWS
+    assert wvsplitk_rows == ([] if padded or rows > 5 else [rows])
+    assert got.shape == (rows, VOCAB_SHARD)
+    want = x.to(torch.bfloat16).float() @ w.to(torch.bfloat16).float().T
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got.float(), want, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+
+def test_draft_lm_head_passes_on_a_rank_without_logits(monkeypatch):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import draft_lm_head
+
+    _skip_unless_gfx942()
+    # The logits processor returns None on a rank that does not get the
+    # gathered logits. The padded path must return None there too, instead
+    # of slicing it.
+    x = torch.zeros(draft_lm_head.ROWS, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    seen: list[int] = []
+
+    def processor(head, h):
+        seen.append(h.shape[0])
+        return None
+
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=True)
+    try:
+        assert draft_lm_head.compute_logits(processor, None, x) is None
+    finally:
+        _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=False)
+    assert seen == [draft_lm_head.ROWS + 1]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""fused_markov.sample_sequential against vLLM's
+DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential.
+
+Both paths run on the same random Markov head, base logits and sampling
+state, for 1 and 2 requests at temperatures 0, 0.6 and 1.0. vLLM's bias is
+the server's GEMV (rocm_unquantized_gemm). The fused launch adds the bias's
+256 products in another order, so a bias value can differ in its last bf16
+bit, and then a draft token can differ. That changes only what the draft
+proposes, because the rejection sampler checks every draft token against the
+target. So against vLLM's loop the test allows at most 1 in 1000 cached
+logits of each request and draft step to differ, and a draft token may differ
+only when a cached logit of its own step differed.
+
+The sampling itself is checked exactly. Each fused draft token must be the
+token that vLLM's sampler (DSparkSpeculator._sample_logits) draws from the
+logits that the fused launch cached for that request and step.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="the fused launch is for ROCm"
+)
+
+VOCAB, RANK, N_SPEC, MAX_REQS = 129280, 256, 5, 4
+
+
+def _set_gate(monkeypatch, on: bool):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import ops
+
+    # The model records --monokernel when it is created. These tests have no
+    # model, so they set the recorded flag themselves.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "_monokernel", on)
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+
+
+class _MarkovW2(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, w):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+            UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+        )
+
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+        self.quant_method = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+
+
+class _Model:
+    """The parts of the DSpark draft model that the sampling uses. The base
+    logits are fixed, so both paths sample from the same ones."""
+
+    def __init__(self, w1, w2, base):
+        head = torch.nn.Module()
+        head.markov_w1 = torch.nn.Embedding(VOCAB, RANK, _weight=w1)
+        head.markov_w2 = _MarkovW2(w2)
+        self.model = SimpleNamespace(markov_head=head)
+        self.base = base
+
+    def compute_draft_logits(self, hidden):
+        return self.base[: hidden.shape[0]]
+
+    def markov_embed(self, ids):
+        return self.model.markov_head.markov_w1(ids)
+
+    def markov_bias(self, e):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import rocm_unquantized_gemm
+
+        w2 = self.model.markov_head.markov_w2
+        return rocm_unquantized_gemm(w2, e, w2.weight, None)
+
+    def map_draft_to_target(self, ids):
+        return ids
+
+
+def _speculator(temp: float, seed: int):
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.speculator import DSparkSpeculator
+
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    bf16 = torch.bfloat16
+    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
+    w1 = torch.randn(VOCAB, RANK, generator=g, device=dev).to(bf16)
+    w2 = (torch.randn(VOCAB, RANK, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.05).to(bf16)
+    base = torch.randn(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, VOCAB, generator=g, device=dev) * 3
+    s = DSparkSpeculator.__new__(DSparkSpeculator)
+    s.model = _Model(w1, w2, base.to(bf16))
+    s.num_speculative_steps = N_SPEC
+    s._draft_topk = None
+    s.use_confidence_head = False
+    s.acceptance_estimator = None
+    s.draft_watermarker = None
+    s._d2t_scatter_index = None
+    s._draft_scatter_buf = None
+    s.use_fp64_gumbel = False
+    s.draft_logits = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, N_SPEC, VOCAB, dtype=bf16, device=dev)
+    s.temperature = torch.full((MAX_REQS,), temp, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
+    s.seeds = torch.randint(0, 2**62, (MAX_REQS,), generator=g, device=dev)
+    s._step_cols = torch.arange(N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    s.sample_indices = torch.arange(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    # Request slots in another order than the rows, and positions past a
+    # long context, as in the server.
+    slots = torch.tensor([2, 0, 3, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    s.sample_idx_mapping = slots.repeat_interleave(N_SPEC)
+    ctx = torch.tensor([131072, 40000, 7, 99999], dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    steps = torch.arange(N_SPEC, device=dev)
+    s.sample_pos = (ctx[:, None] + 1 + steps[None, :]).flatten()
+    s.input_buffers = SimpleNamespace(
+        input_ids=torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (MAX_REQS * N_SPEC,), generator=g, device=dev)
+    )
+    s._anchor_idx = torch.arange(MAX_REQS, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev) * N_SPEC
+    s.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    return s
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("temp", [0.0, 0.6, 1.0])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 2])
+def test_fused_markov_matches_vllm_loop(monkeypatch, num_reqs, temp):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import fused_markov
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.speculator import DSparkSpeculator
+
+    s = _speculator(temp, seed=int(temp * 10) + num_reqs)
+    hidden = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, 8, device="cuda")
+
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=False)
+    DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential(s, num_reqs, hidden)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref_tok, ref_cache = s.draft_tokens.clone(), s.draft_logits.clone()
+
+    s.draft_tokens.zero_()
+    s.draft_logits.zero_()
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=True)
+    try:
+        assert fused_markov.sample_sequential(s, num_reqs, hidden)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    finally:
+        _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=False)
+    got_tok, got_cache = s.draft_tokens.clone(), s.draft_logits.clone()
+
+    # rc and gc are [num_reqs, N_SPEC, VOCAB]: the cached logits of each
+    # request and draft step. The differences are counted for each request
+    # and step, so that a rounding difference in one step cannot excuse a
+    # wrong token in another.
+    slots = s.sample_idx_mapping[: num_reqs * N_SPEC : N_SPEC].long()
+    rc, gc = ref_cache[slots], got_cache[slots]
+    step_diff = (rc.view(torch.int16) != gc.view(torch.int16)).sum(dim=-1)
+    assert int(step_diff.max()) <= VOCAB // 1000, (
+        f"cached logits that differ, by request and draft step: {step_diff.tolist()}"
+    )
+    tok_diff = ref_tok[:num_reqs] != got_tok[:num_reqs]
+    unexplained = (tok_diff & (step_diff == 0)).nonzero().tolist()
+    assert not unexplained, (
+        f"draft tokens differ at (request, step) {unexplained}, "
+        "while every cached logit of that step is equal"
+    )
+
+    # Each fused token must be exactly the token that vLLM's sampler draws
+    # from the logits that the fused launch cached for its request and step,
+    # with the same request slot, seed, position, temperature and cache
+    # column. This checks the sampling of every step without the bias GEMV,
+    # whose rounding may differ. _sample_logits writes the logits it gets
+    # back into the same cache entries, so the checks above use copies.
+    idx_map = s.sample_idx_mapping[: num_reqs * N_SPEC].view(num_reqs, N_SPEC)
+    pos = s.sample_pos[: num_reqs * N_SPEC].view(num_reqs, N_SPEC)
+    for k in range(N_SPEC):
+        drawn = DSparkSpeculator._sample_logits(
+            s, gc[:, k], idx_map[:, k], pos[:, k], k
+        )
+        fused = got_tok[:num_reqs, k]
+        assert torch.equal(drawn, fused), (
+            f"draft step {k}: the fused launch drew {fused.tolist()}, "
+            f"vLLM's sampler draws {drawn.tolist()} from the same logits"
+        )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The gfx942 indexer op of DeepSeek-V4.1 (gfx942_sparse_attn_indexer in
+vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/sparse_indexer.py) against vLLM's ROCm
+indexer op, rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer, on a decode step.
+
+The gfx942 op runs its own copy of the decode path of vLLM's op, with the
+gfx942 top-512 launches in front of vLLM's kernels, so this test fails when
+the copy and vLLM's op stop agreeing. Both ops get the same FP8 queries, head
+weights and paged indexer cache of one request with its 5 DSpark drafts, as
+the 6 flattened rows that the server's decode indexer uses. The layers are one
+without candidate blocks, layer 20, which writes the candidate blocks of
+layers 24 to 36, and one of those layers, which reads them. The ops must write
+the same candidate blocks and choose the same top-512 columns. Equal values at
+the cut may be chosen differently, and then the chosen values must be the same
+multiset.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _on_gfx942(), reason="the op runs the gfx942 launches"
+)
+
+ROWS, HEADS, DIM, PAGE = 6, 64, 128, 64
+TOPK = 512
+MAX_MODEL_LEN = 1 << 20
+CAND_BLOCKS, CAND_BLOCK = 2048, 8
+PREFIX = "model.layers.24.attn.indexer.k_cache"
+# The index layers of V4.1 have compress ratio 1 or 2. On gfx942 both ratios
+# take AITER's paged logits kernel and the same top-k, so one is enough.
+RATIO = 1
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def gfx942_step(monkeypatch):
+    """Turns on AITER and the gfx942 decode launches for one test, and makes
+    the workspace that vLLM's logits call takes its output from. The model
+    records --monokernel when it is created, and this test has no model, so it
+    sets the recorded flag itself."""
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import ops
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import paged_mqa_logits_module
+    from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import (
+        init_workspace_manager,
+        is_workspace_manager_initialized,
+    )
+
+    if paged_mqa_logits_module() is None:
+        pytest.skip("AITER's paged MQA logits module is not installed")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rocm_aiter_ops, "_AITER_ENABLED", True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "_monokernel", True)
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+    if not is_workspace_manager_initialized():
+        init_workspace_manager(torch.device("cuda"))
+    yield
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+
+
+def _make_step(ctx: int):
+    """FP8 queries, head weights, row lengths, block tables and a paged
+    indexer cache of FP8 keys and FP32 key scales. Row r is the request's
+    token at position ctx - ROWS + r and sees the keys up to its own
+    position."""
+    from aiter import dtypes
+
+    torch.manual_seed(ctx)
+    q = (torch.randn(ROWS, HEADS, DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    weights = torch.randn(ROWS, HEADS, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    lens = torch.arange(ctx - ROWS + 1, ctx + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    used = (ctx + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    num_pages = used + 64
+    tables = torch.zeros(ROWS, MAX_MODEL_LEN // PAGE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    tables[:, :used] = torch.randperm(num_pages, device="cuda")[:used].to(torch.int32)
+    vals = (torch.randn(num_pages, PAGE * DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    scales = torch.rand(num_pages, PAGE, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    kv = torch.cat([vals.view(torch.uint8), scales.view(torch.uint8)], dim=1)
+    return q, weights, lens, tables, kv.view(num_pages, PAGE, DIM + 4)
+
+
+def _use_metadata(monkeypatch, lens: torch.Tensor, tables: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Gives both ops the metadata of a step of only decode rows, which the
+    model runner passes through the forward context. Each of the 6 rows is
+    its own decode row of length 1, as in the server's flattened layout."""
+    from vllm.config import CUDAGraphMode
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import sparse_indexer
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import (
+        DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata,
+        DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops import rocm_aiter_mla_sparse
+
+    decode = DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata(
+        block_table=tables,
+        seq_lens=lens,
+        decode_lens=torch.ones(ROWS, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        requires_padding=False,
+        schedule_metadata=torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    meta = DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata(
+        seq_lens=lens,
+        max_seq_len=int(lens.max()),
+        slot_mapping=torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"),
+        num_decodes=ROWS,
+        num_decode_tokens=ROWS,
+        num_prefills=0,
+        num_prefill_tokens=0,
+        decode=decode,
+    )
+    context = SimpleNamespace(
+        attn_metadata={PREFIX: meta}, cudagraph_runtime_mode=CUDAGraphMode.NONE
+    )
+    for module in (sparse_indexer, rocm_aiter_mla_sparse):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "get_forward_context", lambda: context)
+
+
+def _run(op, step, cand=None, write: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """One call of an indexer op on the step, whose model already wrote the
+    K cache. The -7 marks an entry that the op did not write. vLLM's op
+    first fills the rows with -1, and the gfx942 op skips that fill because
+    its top-k writes every entry."""
+    q, weights, lens, tables, kv = step
+    out = torch.full((ROWS, TOPK), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    op(
+        torch.empty(ROWS, 1, device="cuda"),
+        PREFIX,
+        kv,
+        q,
+        None,
+        weights,
+        128,
+        "ue8m0",
+        TOPK,
+        DIM,
+        MAX_MODEL_LEN,
+        int(lens.sum()),
+        out,
+        skip_k_cache_insert=True,
+        compress_ratio=RATIO,
+        candidate_blocks=cand,
+        candidate_block_size=CAND_BLOCK if cand is not None else 0,
+        candidate_write=write,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def _assert_same_top512(dense, ref, got, ends, cand=None):
+    """Got must hold vLLM's columns, or other columns with the same logits
+    where logits at the cut are equal. With candidate blocks, every column
+    must also lie in one of the row's candidate blocks."""
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):
+        g, w = got[r], ref[r]
+        assert ((g >= -1) & (g < e)).all(), f"row {r}: an entry outside -1 to {e - 1}"
+        gl, wl = g[g >= 0].long(), w[w >= 0].long()
+        assert gl.unique().numel() == gl.numel(), f"row {r}: a column twice"
+        assert gl.numel() == wl.numel(), (
+            f"row {r}: {gl.numel()} columns, vLLM's op {wl.numel()}"
+        )
+        if cand is not None:
+            blocks = cand[r][cand[r] >= 0].long()
+            assert torch.isin(gl // CAND_BLOCK, blocks).all(), (
+                f"row {r}: a column outside the candidate blocks"
+            )
+        if set(gl.tolist()) != set(wl.tolist()):
+            vg = sorted(dense[r, gl].tolist())
+            vw = sorted(dense[r, wl].tolist())
+            assert vg == vw, f"row {r}: different top-512 logits"
+
+
+def _block_scores(row: torch.Tensor, end: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """VLLM's block scores of one row before its end: the largest logit of a
+    block, and +inf for the newest block."""
+    nblocks = math.ceil(end / CAND_BLOCK)
+    padded = torch.full((nblocks * CAND_BLOCK,), -math.inf, device=row.device)
+    padded[:end] = row[:end]
+    scores = padded.view(nblocks, CAND_BLOCK).amax(dim=1)
+    scores[-1] = math.inf
+    return scores.cpu()
+
+
+def _assert_same_candidates(dense, ref, got, ends):
+    """Got must hold vLLM's candidate blocks in any order, or other blocks
+    with the same scores where scores at the cut are equal."""
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):
+        w, g = ref[r].tolist(), got[r].tolist()
+        ws, gs = sorted(v for v in w if v >= 0), sorted(v for v in g if v >= 0)
+        assert min(g) >= -1, f"row {r}: an entry below -1"
+        assert len(gs) == len(set(gs)), f"row {r}: a block id twice"
+        assert w.count(-1) == g.count(-1), f"row {r}: different -1 counts"
+        if ws != gs:
+            scores = _block_scores(dense[r], e)
+            assert sorted(scores[ws].tolist()) == sorted(scores[gs].tolist()), (
+                f"row {r}: different chosen block scores"
+            )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ctx", [8192, 131072])
+def test_decode_step_matches_vllm_op(gfx942_step, monkeypatch, ctx):
+    """At 8192 tokens a row has 1024 blocks of 8, so all of them are
+    candidates. At 131072 tokens a row has 16384 blocks, and 2048 of them
+    are candidates."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import sparse_indexer, topk
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer,
+        rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits,
+    )
+
+    step = _make_step(ctx)
+    q, weights, lens, tables, kv = step
+    _use_metadata(monkeypatch, lens, tables)
+    # Record that the gfx942 op ran its decode path and that the gfx942
+    # launches of layer 20 and of layers 24 to 36 took their calls, so that
+    # the test cannot pass on vLLM's kernels alone.
+    taken = []
+
+    def recorder(real, name):
+        def record(*args, **kwargs):
+            out = real(*args, **kwargs)
+            if out is not False:
+                taken.append(name)
+            return out
+
+        return record
+
+    for module, name in (
+        (sparse_indexer, "_decode_step"),
+        (topk, "select_candidates"),
+        (topk, "candidate_logits_top_k"),
+    ):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(module, name, recorder(getattr(module, name), name))
+
+    dense = rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(
+        q.view(ROWS, 1, HEADS, DIM),
+        kv.unsqueeze(-2),
+        weights,
+        lens,
+        tables,
+        torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        max_model_len=MAX_MODEL_LEN,
+        compress_ratio=RATIO,
+    ).clone()
+    ends = lens.tolist()
+    vllm_op = rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer
+    gfx942_op = sparse_indexer.gfx942_sparse_attn_indexer
+
+    # A layer without candidate blocks.
+    ref = _run(vllm_op, step)
+    got = _run(gfx942_op, step)
+    _assert_same_top512(dense, ref, got, ends)
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The gfx942 top-512 helpers of the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse indexer
+(vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/topk.py) against vLLM's ops.
+
+Each helper must choose the columns or blocks that vLLM's op chooses. Equal
+values at the cut may be chosen differently, and then the chosen values must
+be the same multiset. The steps are one request with its 5 DSpark drafts,
+3 such requests, and 8 requests without drafts. The logits rows are as wide
+as the AgentX server's max_model_len (1M).
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _on_gfx942(), reason="the extension is built for gfx942"
+)
+
+WIDTH = 1 << 20
+TOPK_BLOCKS, BLOCK = 2048, 8
+# (requests, rows a request) of a decode step.
+STEPS = [(1, 6), (3, 6), (8, 1)]
+STEP_IDS = ["1x6", "3x6", "8x1"]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def gfx942_decode(monkeypatch):
+    """Turns on the gfx942 decode helpers for one test. The model records
+    --monokernel when it is created, and this test has no model, so it sets
+    the recorded flag itself."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import ops
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "_monokernel", True)
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+    yield
+    ops.enabled.cache_clear()
+
+
+def _lengths(length: int, reqs: int) -> list[int]:
+    """The requests' lengths: the first is ``length`` and the others are
+    shorter by a few hundred tokens each, so the rows end at different
+    places."""
+    return [max(0, length - 397 * i) for i in range(reqs)]
+
+
+def _seq_lens(lengths: list[int], next_n: int, layout: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The lengths per row (2d) or per request (1d), the two forms that
+    vLLM's decode indexer uses."""
+    if layout == "2d":
+        ends = [max(0, n - next_n + 1 + j) for n in lengths for j in range(next_n)]
+        return torch.tensor(ends, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(-1, next_n)
+    return torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+
+def _row_ends(seq_lens: torch.Tensor, next_n: int, rows: int) -> list[int]:
+    """Each row's end, the way vLLM's top_k_per_row_decode computes it."""
+    lens = seq_lens.reshape(-1).tolist()
+    if seq_lens.dim() == 2:
+        return [max(0, v) for v in lens[:rows]]
+    return [max(0, lens[r // next_n] - next_n + r % next_n + 1) for r in range(rows)]
+
+
+def _visible(seq_lens: torch.Tensor, next_n: int, rows: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The int64 row ends that vLLM's decode indexer passes to its candidate
+    kernels."""
+    visible = seq_lens.reshape(-1)
+    if visible.numel() != rows:
+        visible = visible.repeat_interleave(next_n)
+    return visible[:rows].to(torch.int64)
+
+
+def _row_sets(indices: torch.Tensor, ends: list[int]) -> list[set[int]]:
+    out = []
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):
+        got = indices[r, :512]
+        live = got[got >= 0]
+        assert (live < e).all(), f"row {r}: an index past the row end {e}"
+        assert live.unique().numel() == live.numel(), f"row {r}: repeated indices"
+        out.append(set(live.tolist()))
+    return out
+
+
+def _assert_same_top512(x, ref, got, ends, name):
+    """Got must hold vLLM's columns, or other columns with the same values
+    where values at the cut are equal, and -1 past a short row's end."""
+    want, have = _row_sets(ref, ends), _row_sets(got, ends)
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):
+        pad = got[r, min(512, e) :]
+        assert (pad == -1).all(), f"{name} row {r}: missing -1 padding"
+        if have[r] != want[r]:
+            vg = sorted(x[r, list(have[r])].tolist())
+            vw = sorted(x[r, list(want[r])].tolist())
+            assert vg == vw, f"{name} row {r}: different top-512 values"
+
+
+def _logits(ends: list[int], masked: bool, gen) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Random logits. ``masked`` keeps 2047 random blocks of 8 and the newest
+    block of each row and sets the rest of the row to -inf, as layers 24 to
+    36 see their logits after the DSpark candidate mask."""
+    x = torch.randn(len(ends), WIDTH, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 4.0
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):
+        nblocks = (e + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+        if not masked or nblocks <= TOPK_BLOCKS:
+            continue
+        keep = torch.zeros(nblocks, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+        pick = torch.randperm(nblocks - 1, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        keep[pick[: TOPK_BLOCKS - 1]] = True
+        keep[nblocks - 1] = True
+        live = keep.repeat_interleave(BLOCK)[:e]
+        x[r, :e] = torch.where(live, x[r, :e], float("-inf"))
+    return x
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("register_select", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("masked", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [100, 517, 16384, 131072, 300000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reqs,next_n", STEPS, ids=STEP_IDS)
+def test_decode_top_k_matches_vllm(reqs, next_n, length, masked, register_select):
+    from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import topk
+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(length + reqs)
+    rows = reqs * next_n
+    seq_lens = _seq_lens(_lengths(length, reqs), next_n, "2d")
+    ends = _row_ends(seq_lens, next_n, rows)
+    x = _logits(ends, masked, gen)
+    ref = torch.full((rows, 512), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    got = torch.full_like(ref, -7)
+    ops.top_k_per_row_decode(
+        x, next_n, seq_lens, ref, rows, x.stride(0), x.stride(1), 512
+    )
+    topk.top_k_per_row_decode_512(
+        x, next_n, seq_lens, got, register_select=register_select
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_same_top512(x, ref, got, ends, f"length {length}")
+
+
+def _compact_rows(kind: str, rows: int, length: int, gen) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if kind == "normal":
+        return torch.randn(rows, length, generator=gen)
+    if kind == "wide":
+        return torch.randn(rows, length, generator=gen) * torch.exp(
+            torch.randn(rows, length, generator=gen) * 4
+        )
+    if kind == "few values":
+        return torch.randint(0, 40, (rows, length), generator=gen).float()
+    if kind == "all equal":
+        return torch.full((rows, length), 0.75)
+    if kind == "near max":
+        # Most values sit just below the largest, so the first pass of
+        # selectFromRegisters, which bins by sign, exponent and the top 5
+        # mantissa bits, puts the whole row in one bin.
+        return 1000.0 - torch.rand(rows, length, generator=gen) * 1e-3
+    x = torch.randn(rows, length, generator=gen)
+    x[:, 1000:1500] = float("-inf")
+    x[2, : length - 1000] = float("-inf")
+    x[3, : length - 300] = float("-inf")
+    return x
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kind", ["normal", "wide", "few values", "all equal", "near max", "with -inf"]
+)
+def test_compact_register_select_matches_radix_job(kind):
+    """compact_top_k_512_regs (selectFromRegisters) against
+    compact_top_k_512 (vLLM's topKPerRowJob) on compact candidate rows of 16384
+    logits, whose ids are their positions."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import topk
+
+    ext = topk._load()
+    rows, length = 6, TOPK_BLOCKS * BLOCK
+    x = _compact_rows(kind, rows, length, torch.Generator().manual_seed(3))
+    logits = x.cuda().contiguous()
+    ids = torch.arange(length, dtype=torch.int32).repeat(rows, 1).cuda()
+    lens = torch.full((rows,), 1 << 20, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    old = torch.empty(rows, 512, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    new = torch.empty_like(old)
+    ext.compact_top_k_512(logits, ids, lens, 1, old)
+    ext.compact_top_k_512_regs(logits, ids, lens, 1, new)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    old, new = old.cpu(), new.cpu()
+    top = torch.topk(x, 512, dim=1).values
+    for r in range(rows):
+        pos = new[r].long()
+        assert pos.min() >= 0 and pos.unique().numel() == 512, f"row {r}"
+        chosen = torch.sort(x[r, pos], descending=True).values
+        assert torch.equal(chosen, top[r]), f"row {r}: not the 512 largest values"
+        cut = top[r, -1]
+        if int((x[r] == cut).sum()) == int((top[r] == cut).sum()):
+            # Without equal values at the cut the set is unique.
+            assert torch.equal(new[r].sort().values, old[r].sort().values), f"row {r}"
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["2d", "1d"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [100, 512, 517, 16390, 131072, 300000])

+    candidate lists come from vLLM's own block selection over another row,
+    as layer 20 writes them."""

+        _select_candidate_blocks,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops import topk
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        _apply_candidate_mask_strided,
+    )

+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(length + reqs + len(layout))
+    rows = reqs * next_n
+    seq_lens = _seq_lens(_lengths(length, reqs), next_n, layout)
+    ends = _row_ends(seq_lens, next_n, rows)
+    visible = _visible(seq_lens, next_n, rows)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, WIDTH, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 4.0
+    src = torch.randn(rows, WIDTH, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 4.0
+    cand = torch.empty(rows, TOPK_BLOCKS, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    _select_candidate_blocks(
+        src, torch.zeros_like(visible), visible, TOPK_BLOCKS, BLOCK, cand

+    got = torch.full_like(ref, -7)

+    )
+    ops.top_k_per_row_decode(
+        masked, next_n, seq_lens, ref, rows, masked.stride(0), masked.stride(1), 512
+    )
+    assert topk.candidate_top_k(x, next_n, seq_lens, cand, BLOCK, got, 512)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    for r, e in enumerate(ends):

+            # must hold columns 0 to end - 1 and then -1.

+def _block_scores(row: torch.Tensor, end: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """VLLM's block scores of one row before its end: the largest logit of a
+    block (NaN when the block holds a NaN), and +inf for the newest block."""
+    nblocks = math.ceil(end / BLOCK)
+    padded = torch.full((nblocks * BLOCK,), -math.inf, device=row.device)
+    padded[:end] = row[:end]
+    scores = padded.view(nblocks, BLOCK).amax(dim=1)
+    if end > 0:
+        scores[-1] = math.inf
+    return scores.cpu()
+
+
+def _sort_key(v: float):
+    # NaN sorts above +inf, as torch.topk and vLLM's topKPerRowJob pick it.
+    return (1, 0.0) if v != v else (0, v)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", ["random", "ties", "special"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["2d", "1d"])

+

+    rows = reqs * next_n
+    seq_lens = _seq_lens(_lengths(length, reqs), next_n, layout)
+    visible = _visible(seq_lens, next_n, rows)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, WIDTH, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 4.0
+    if case == "ties":
+        x = torch.round(x * 2.0) / 2.0
+    elif case == "special":
+        cols = torch.randint(0, WIDTH, (rows, 16), device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        x.scatter_(1, cols, math.nan)
+        blocks = torch.randint(
+            0, WIDTH // BLOCK, (rows, 64), device="cuda", generator=gen
+        )
+        for j in range(BLOCK):
+            x.scatter_(1, blocks * BLOCK + j, -math.inf)
+    ref = torch.full((rows, TOPK_BLOCKS), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    got = torch.full_like(ref, -7)

+    )

+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()

+        assert len(gs) == len(set(gs)), f"row {r}: a block id twice"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""The gfx942 parts of the DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode kernels
+(vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono) on the GPU.
+
+  key lists  keylist.launch, which writes K2's key lists on an index layer,
+             against a reference built in torch from its documented format.
+  entry seam AITER's delayed seam on the expanded residual, which the first
+             layer uses with the mono layers on, against vLLM's torch seam
+             on the folded weight.
+  GEMV       the attention GEMV core (attention/gemv.py) and the MoE side's
+             FP8 GEMV (stages/gemv.py) on the gfx942 weight copy
+             (weights942.dense_copy), against a float64 product.
+  MoE        the FNUZ conversion helpers, the bf16 MFMA built from two
+             MFMAs, the routed experts' up/gate GEMV and their down
+             projection on the gfx942 copy, against float64 references.
+
+The test kernels call the same device functions as K1 and K2, one function
+at a time, on random inputs of the model's shapes.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+if not _on_gfx942():
+    pytest.skip("the gfx942 mono kernels need a gfx942 GPU", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytest.importorskip("flydsl")
+pytest.importorskip("aiter")

+import flydsl.compiler as flyc  # noqa: E402
+import flydsl.expr as fx  # noqa: E402
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo  # noqa: E402
+from flydsl.expr import const_expr, gpu, range_constexpr  # noqa: E402
+from flydsl.expr.typing import Int64, T  # noqa: E402
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.attention import gemv as G  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.attention.device import (  # noqa: E402
+    THREADS,
+    WAVES,
+    fp8x8_bf16,
+    rsrc,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.common.gfx942 import (  # noqa: E402
+    fp4x8_fnuz,
+    mfma_bf16_k32,
+    ocp_to_fnuz,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.stages import gemv as SG  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.stages import moe as M  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.weights942 import (  # noqa: E402
+    EVEN_ODD,
+    codes_tile_rounds,
+    dense_copy,
+    fp4_drop_negative_zero_,
+    fp4_tile_major,
+)

+HIDDEN = 5120
+E2M1 = torch.tensor(
+    [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0]
+    + [-0.0, -0.5, -1.0, -1.5, -2.0, -3.0, -4.0, -6.0],
+    dtype=torch.float64,
+)

+
+def _ld(ptr, i, n=1):
+    v = bo.buffer_load(rsrc(ptr), i, vec_width=n, dtype=T.i32)
+    return fx.Int32(v) if n == 1 else fx.Vector(v)
+
+
+def _st(v, ptr, i):
+    bo.buffer_store(v, rsrc(ptr), i)
+
+
+def _rel_err(got: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return (got.double() - ref).abs().max().item() / ref.abs().max().item()
+
+
+# Key lists
+
+
+def _keylist_reference(slot, pos, swa_idx, swa_lens, t2r, ratio, topk, bt, cb):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.attention.plan import KEYS, TOPK
+
+    S = slot.shape[0]
+    kt = torch.full((S, KEYS), -1, dtype=torch.int64)
+    klen = torch.zeros(2 * S, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for t in range(S):
+        live = int(slot[t]) >= 0
+        nswa = int(swa_lens[t]) if live else 0
+        ntopk = min((int(pos[t]) + 1) // ratio, TOPK) if live and ratio else 0
+        for k in range(ntopk):
+            local = int(topk[t, k])
+            if local >= 0:
+                # The kernel sets bit 31 of the int32 slot. For a slot below
+                # 2^31 that is the slot minus 2^31.
+                blk = int(bt[int(t2r[t]), local // cb])
+                kt[t, k] = blk * cb + local % cb - (1 << 31)

+        klen[t], klen[S + t] = ntopk + nswa, ntopk
+    return kt.to(torch.int32).view(-1), klen

+def test_entry_seam_matches_torch():
+    """VLLM projects the first layer's 2-D embedding x with the sum of
+    hc_attn_fn over the hc copies. With the mono layers on, the seam projects
+    the expanded residual (hc equal copies of x) with hc_attn_fn itself. The
+    two are the same sum with the products added in another order, and the
+    layer input is the same bit for bit."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.mhc.aiter import mhc_pre_delayed_aiter
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.mhc.torch import mhc_pre_delayed_torch
+
+    hc, iters = 4, 20
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    hc3 = hc * (2 + hc)
+    fn = torch.randn(hc3, hc * HIDDEN, device="cuda") * 0.02
+    scale = torch.tensor([0.5, 0.7, 0.9], device="cuda")
+    base = torch.randn(hc3, device="cuda") * 0.1
+    x = (torch.randn(6, HIDDEN, device="cuda") * 3).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    residual = x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hc, -1).contiguous()
+    folded = fn.view(hc3, hc, HIDDEN).sum(dim=1)
+    eps = (1e-6, 1e-6, 1e-6)
+    ref = mhc_pre_delayed_torch(
+        residual, folded, scale, base, *eps, 2.0, iters, pre_mix=None, x=x
+    )
+    new = mhc_pre_delayed_aiter(
+        residual, fn, scale, base, *eps, 2.0, iters, pre_mix=None
+    )
+    names = ("post_mix", "comb_mix", "layer_input", "next_pre_mix")
+    for name, a, b in zip(names, ref, new):
+        a, b = a.float().reshape(-1), b.float().reshape(-1)
+        if name == "layer_input":
+            assert torch.equal(a, b), name
+        else:
+            assert _rel_err(b, a.double()) < 1e-4, name
