I can approve the PR once we are confident if gfx950 is still intact. @simondanielsson Thanks for the abstraction, currently we need to be cautious with moving the files under the common folder as cross-model-family sharing still needs more validation, e.g. cross-check between DeepSeek and Kimi hasn't been done yet, for now let's keep everything within its own model folder to avoid any potential conflicts.

@Fangzhou-Ai I ran `main` and this PR twice each on the same MI355X node, in the order PR, `main`, `main`, PR. All four runs use `--monokernel` at TP2, DSpark with 5 drafts, probabilistic drafts and block rejection, and the same server arguments. `main` is the nightly image of 39983a5e, and the PR runs use the same image with this PR's files at 6caadd0 copied in. The commits after 6caadd0 change no code that runs on gfx950, because their hooks return early unless `ops.enabled()`, which needs gfx942.

| | `main`, run 1 | `main`, run 2 | This PR, run 1 | This PR, run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, strict match | 0.9249 | 0.9272 | 0.9257 | 0.9242 |
| Concurrency 1, output throughput (tokens/s) | 520.34 | 579.54 | 584.43 | 577.95 |
| Concurrency 1, median TPOT (ms) | 1.59 | 1.56 | 1.54 | 1.48 |
| Concurrency 1, median ITL (ms) | 7.60 | 7.59 | 7.36 | 7.38 |
| Concurrency 1, median TTFT (ms) | 66.30 | 66.55 | 67.09 | 67.02 |
| Concurrency 8, output throughput (tokens/s) | 2038.63 | 1986.51 | 2049.16 | 2099.40 |
| Concurrency 8, median TPOT (ms) | 3.37 | 3.35 | 3.47 | 3.17 |
| Concurrency 8, median ITL (ms) | 17.06 | 16.99 | 16.84 | 16.77 |
| Concurrency 8, median TTFT (ms) | 84.37 | 83.77 | 84.51 | 83.91 |

The speed rows use random prompts of 1024 tokens and 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at concurrency 1 and 64 at concurrency 8. GSM8K is the same within the spread of the runs, and the median TTFT differs by less than 1 ms. With DSpark a decode step streams several tokens, so the median ITL is the time of one decode step. This PR's decode steps are about 0.2 ms shorter at both concurrencies, in both runs. That comes from the padding loops of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, which this PR changes on every platform (see Details in the description), because DSpark runs that kernel once for each draft KV cache group in every decode step. The TPOT also depends on how many drafts are accepted, so at concurrency 8 it moves between 3.17 and 3.47 ms over the four runs. In the first `main` run a few first tokens took more than a second, which lowered its throughput at concurrency 1. So the gfx950 path is intact.

On the folders: this PR keeps all of its kernels in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`.

The new `test_dsv41_gfx942_sparse_indexer.py` runs the layer and vLLM's op on the same decode step and fails when the two stop agreeing.
- The DSpark speculator no longer imports DSv4.1 code. It asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, and only the DSv4.1 draft model has one.
- The `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change is dropped. #58633 parallelises the same padding loops, and this PR does not need it.

Outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and the tests, the PR changes only that 8-line hook in the DSpark speculator and adds the two MI300 CI jobs.

The branch also merges `main` with #62131. On gfx950 the draft layers run as #62131 runs them. On gfx942 they keep the FFN launch after vLLM's attention.

@Fangzhou-Ai, the merge found a bug in #62131. Its draft runner builds the MoE with `DRAFT_UG_GROUPS = 1`, but `scratch_layout` sizes the MoE regions for the default two groups, and with one group the `ugf` flags take twice the room. So the flags of the upper half of the ug tasks are written over the start of the `normed` rows, which the draft MoE reads as its input, at TP 2 and 4 and for every step width. The target's output is not affected. c688ebe passes the runner's `ug_groups` to `scratch_layout` and `scratch_bytes`. This PR checks that each MoE region of a build fits the layout, and that check stopped the build of the draft runner's K2, so the fix has to come with this PR. On MI355X at TP2 with `--monokernel`, servers of `main` and of c688ebe both ran the draft layers whole and answered the sanity prompts correctly, and on GSM8K they accepted as many drafts, so the overlap did not show in the drafts there.

The checks of 6cb1400 are at the end of Validation in the description.
/ci run

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #95911](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95911) for commit `4d0efb49acbc`.

ℹ️ This PR is 42 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `4d0efb49acbc` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

reviews.body:
_Preliminary AI-assisted review. The analysis and testing were done with Claude Code (Opus 5.5 and GLM 5.3); I reviewed the results._

_As on #60397, this is an actively developing area, so these are suggestions ranked by how strongly I'd recommend them, not a checklist. The #60397 review comments carry over here and aren't repeated; its author has since pushed the deployment checks and test hardening there (dea9fa3b95, b9423a8c7d), which this branch doesn't have yet._

Thanks for this, and for the very thorough description. Tested on **MI300X** (192 GiB, 4 GPUs): this branch installed into `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-8cbd5d0300` (covers the merge-base). All 237 new gfx942 kernel tests pass on MI300X. E2E with the description's server command, adapted (block rejection, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 96`):

| | mono off | mono on |
|---|---|---|
| Weights per rank | 98.88 GiB | 169.07 GiB |
| KV cache | 63.79 GiB, 4.15M tokens (util 0.9) | **fails at util 0.9** (−8.25 GiB); 2.31 GiB, 149K tokens at 0.955 |
| Single request, 512 tokens, mean ITL | 6.10 ms | 2.70 ms (2.26×) |
| Kernels per decode period (torch profiler, rank 0) | 1,885 | 342; K1 ~24 µs, K2 93–97 µs, draft FFN launch 52 µs |
| GSM8K 5-shot, first 400, greedy, concurrency 1 | 0.930 ± 0.013 | 0.950 ± 0.011 |

So the speedup, kernel counts and accuracy match the description on MI300X too.

### Would like to see before merge

**1. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is JIT-built with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load` at the first decode step.** vLLM builds its kernels through `csrc/` and CMake; a runtime hipcc build needs hipcc and a writable extension cache at serve time, fails mid-serving instead of at startup, and has no fallback. Please move it into `csrc/` (or at least build at startup with a fallback to `top_k_per_row_decode`).

**2. `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` fails 6 of 26 with this PR**, none of them hardware-dependent: the CDNA message is now "needs CDNA3/4", the mocks lack `layer.engram`, `runner.ffn()` takes `topk`, and a path needs the TP group. It runs in the MI355 Basic Models step, so CI goes red once it runs.

**3. MI300X doesn't really fit.** With the copies, the description's own `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` fails at startup on MI300X; the ceiling is ~0.955 (only ~184 of 192 GiB free at worker startup), leaving 2.31 GiB of KV — 149K tokens, about two 64K requests, and not one at the recipe's 1M context. Most of the +70 GiB is the routed-expert copies (~69 GiB). I'd scope the claims to MI325X, or document the MI300X limits.

**4. The rebase onto #60397's new head needs care.** The parent's new `MonoLayerWeights.check` asserts the gfx950 layout (fp4x2 `w13`, E8M0 block scales, padded intermediate); on gfx942 the tensors are the `weights942` copies (FNUZ bytes, tile-major, padding cut), so the check needs a gfx942 variant or the copies go unchecked — the exact gap the parent's fix closed. The unit test file also changed there (new MoE-rejection and padded-step cases), so it's a reconcile, not just fixing the 6 failures.

### Recommended, fine as follow-ups

**5. Reloaded weights don't reach the copies.** `_capture_plain_experts` skips the rebuild when `mono942` exists, and the dense copies are cached on first use, so after `reload_weights` or an RL weight update, prefill uses the new weights while ≤6-row decode silently uses the old ones. Captured graphs hold the copies' pointers, so a fix would `copy_` into them in place.

**6. The two changes outside the switch** (the `wvSplitK` ≤4 rows on gfx942 for every model, and the DFlash padding on every platform) each have a single measurement behind them. They'd be easier to land and to bisect as their own small PRs.

### Nits

- The dense copies (~1.8 GiB) are built at the first eager decode step, which by default is the cudagraph memory-profiling pass, so they're counted as graph memory (estimate 5.74 GiB with mono vs 3.40 without). That works, but only by accident: with graph-memory profiling off or `enforce_eager` they'd escape accounting. Building them at load would be clearer.
- `common/arch.py` decides `GFX942` from the `ARCH` env var, while `_on_gfx942()` asks the platform. A stray `ARCH` (a generic name) can make the weight copies and the kernel builds disagree.
- A gfx942 twin of the parent's new 300-replay graph stress (both widths, one graph, bit for bit) would guard the FNUZ copies' path; the shadow mode (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW`) already provides the harness.

For what it's worth, the FNUZ re-encoding traced as exact: the bf16 → e4m3 round trip, the halved bit patterns with scale code +1, subnormals and −0. The checkpoint's scale codes (dense 109–121, experts 115–127) are well clear of the E8M0 edge cases.
